title: The API test layer
bridge: The new API test layer is like adding a Vitest project next to an older Jest suite. It gets its own folder, config file and CI job. The old tests keep running as they are. Except: every test here sends a real request through Django into a real Postgres copy. So the slow part is the database, and the design is about making that fast.
intro: G7 starts with one folder in fcp: cloud/rhinoCloud/tests_api/. It holds pytest tests that call the cloud's API in-process. It is built for speed: a full run in about 3 minutes on a laptop, the affected tests in under 30 seconds. This lesson walks through its five tickets: the decision, the database setup, the CI job, the agent report and testmon.

picture.caption: One edit, one fast answer: a template database copied per worker, and one page per failure.

nodes.label: Agent or engineer edits cloud code

steps.text: runs the tests after an edit (only the affected ones with testmon)
the first worker takes a lock and migrates the template once
each xdist worker gets CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE, a copy in seconds
the tests run; the controller writes one short block per failure
the agent reads failures.md and reruns one test with the printed command
the push runs the same layer as the API Tests job, with a throw-away Postgres

p: Open cloud/rhinoCloud in fcp. rhinoCore/tests holds about 1,900 unit tests that run with Django's own runner, manage.py test, on CommonRhinoTestCase and factory_boy. rhinoCore/integration-tests holds pytest tests that run against shared QA, where a push waits 20 to 30 minutes for a lock. Nothing in between gives a fast answer about an endpoint.

G7-01 is a 30-minute meeting with the BE guild and Shai (the G7 design lead), and its output is a written decision. Tests that call an endpoint and check the response go to tests_api/ on pytest, pytest-django and xdist. Model and service unit tests stay in rhinoCore/tests. Nobody moves old tests in bulk this quarter.

The rules come from numbers you bring: rhinoCore/tests has 69 mock.patch calls on AgentRpcClient, 24 on StorageService and 11 uses of CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER. So the new layer uses no eager Celery and no mocks of those two classes; lesson g7-2 builds fakes instead. Data is created through the API, and it is fake data only (Faker, factory_boy), never rows copied from QA or prod.

The meeting also fixes the names the next tickets use. Group api-tests; Poe tasks api-test, api-test-affected and verify; CI job "API Tests"; markers contract and sdk_smoke. The speed goals (30 seconds affected, 3 minutes full, 6 minutes in CI with lint) are numbers to watch, not gates. The outcome goes into the testing section of be-repo-conventions/SKILL.md, so agents read the same rules.

callout.text: Why Python and not TypeScript? The agent platform is TypeScript, but fcp's backend is a Django codebase. Its tests, fakes and scripts stay Python, because agents work inside that code. The language of the platform does not change the language of the code it fixes.

sections.h: The conftest, part 1: name the template (G7-02)
p: G7-02 first adds a dependency group to cloud/rhinoCloud/pyproject.toml: api-tests with pytest, pytest-django, pytest-xdist and pytest-randomly, each with a version range. make update-deps refreshes uv.lock, and the sync-deps target in the Makefile gets --group api-tests.

tests_api/ gets its own pytest.ini with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE = rhinoCloud.rhinoDjango.settings, django_find_project = false, the pythonpath entries and the two markers. Because the ini sits inside tests_api/, pytest tests_api never reads cloud/rhinoCloud/pytest.ini, which holds the integration-test markers.

Then the conftest. The problem it solves: rhinoCore has more than 220 migrations, and pytest-django would run all of them once per xdist worker. The conftest migrates one template database instead, and its name comes from the migration file names.
sections.because: We hash the migration names into the template's name, because a new migration must build a new template.

code.text:
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from django.conf import settings
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.db import connection, connections

CORE = Path(__file__).parents[1] / "rhinoCore"
MIGRATIONS = "".join(sorted(p.name for p in (CORE / "migrations").glob("[0-9]*.py")))
TEMPLATE_DB = "api_tpl_" + hashlib.sha1(MIGRATIONS.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]  # a new migration means a new template

notes.text: hashlib gives us sha1, a quick fingerprint of a string.
Path builds file paths with the / operator, like path.join in Node.
settings is the loaded Django settings module; we will change the database name in it.
call_command runs a manage.py command (migrate, loaddata) from Python.
connection is the default database connection; connections holds all of them.
parents[1] is the folder above tests_api/, so CORE points at cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore.
Every migration file name that starts with a digit, sorted and glued into one long string.
api_tpl_ plus the first 12 hex characters of the hash. Add a migration and the name changes, so a fresh template is built.

sections.h: The conftest, part 2: build once, copy per worker
p: pytest-django calls a fixture named django_db_setup once per session to create the test database. We override it. One worker builds the template under a Postgres advisory lock. The others wait on the same lock, then find the template ready. An advisory lock is a named lock in Postgres that your code takes and releases; Postgres attaches no meaning to it.

Then every worker asks Postgres for a copy: CREATE DATABASE test_api_gw1 TEMPLATE api_tpl_<hash>. Postgres copies files on disk, so this takes seconds. pytest-django then wraps each test in a transaction and rolls it back, as in lesson p10-3.
sections.because: We take a lock before checking for the template, because four workers start at once and only one may migrate.

code.text:
@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def django_db_setup(django_db_blocker, worker_id):
    # Migrate once into a template DB, then give each xdist worker its own copy: seconds instead of 228 migrations.
    db = settings.DATABASES["default"]
    worker_db = f"test_api_{worker_id}"  # worker_id is "master" when xdist is off
    with django_db_blocker.unblock(), connection._nodb_cursor() as cur:  # Django's own cursor on the "postgres" DB
        cur.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_lock(7007)")  # one worker builds the template; released when cur closes
        cur.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = %s", [TEMPLATE_DB])
        if cur.fetchone() is None:
            cur.execute(f'CREATE DATABASE "{TEMPLATE_DB}"')
            db["NAME"] = TEMPLATE_DB
            call_command("migrate", verbosity=0)
            call_command("createcachetable")  # settings.CACHES uses the database_cache table
            call_command("loaddata", str(CORE / "fixtures" / "initial_data_prod_aws.json"), verbosity=0)
            connections.close_all()  # CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE needs no open sessions on the template
        cur.execute(f'DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "{worker_db}"')
        cur.execute(f'CREATE DATABASE "{worker_db}" TEMPLATE "{TEMPLATE_DB}"')
    db["NAME"] = worker_db
    yield

notes.text: Session scope: this fixture runs once per worker process, not once per test.
The name pytest-django looks for. django_db_blocker guards database access; worker_id is gw0, gw1, ... (lesson p10-2).
The dict that describes the default database. Changing NAME here changes which database Django opens.
One database per worker, for example test_api_gw2, or test_api_master without xdist.
unblock() allows database access in this block. _nodb_cursor() is Django's own cursor on the server's postgres database, outside any test database.
Take lock 7007. A second worker waits here until the first one's cursor closes.
Ask Postgres whether the template already exists.
Only when it does not exist: build it.
Create the empty template database.
Point Django at the template, so the next commands write into it.
Run every migration once, quietly.
The settings use a database cache table, so create it too.
Load the same seed fixture CommonRhinoTestCase uses, so tests start with the same base rows.
Close every connection. Postgres refuses to copy a template that has open sessions.
Drop this worker's copy from an earlier run, if there is one.
The copy: a full database in seconds instead of more than 220 migrations.
From now on, every test on this worker uses its own copy.
Hand control back to pytest. Nothing to clean up: the next run drops the copy.

callout.text: If a run dies in the middle of building the template, a half-built api_tpl_<hash> stays behind and the next run reuses it. Drop it by hand (DROP DATABASE) if tests fail with missing tables after a crash. The conftest's docstring also says that locally poe cloud-up-debug exposes Postgres on localhost:5431. One more: the tickets count 228 migrations, and the branch had 224 when this was written. The number only explains the speed-up, so never hard-code it.

sections.h: The CI job, part 1: env and Postgres (G7-03)
p: The layer must run on every push, not only on laptops. G7-03 adds a job called API Tests to .github/workflows/cloud-ci.yml. It copies the shape of the existing test job: the same runner, needs and if lines, and the same Postgres service container. A service container is one that GitHub Actions starts next to the job and removes after it.
Remember that cloud-ci.yml runs on push to any branch, not on pull_request (lesson p2-1). check-changes is the reusable job that says whether this push touched cloud code.
sections.because: We copy the test job's env and Postgres service, because settings read those variables at import time.

code.text:
api-tests:
    name: API Tests
    runs-on: fcp-runner-set
    needs: check-changes
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || needs.check-changes.outputs.has_changes == 'true'
    env:
      ENV: QA
      RHINO_IS_RUNNING_UNIT_TESTS: 1
      POSTGRES_HOST: localhost
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CLOUD_TEST_POSTGRES_PASSWORD }}
      # ...the rest of the `test` job's env block (a YAML anchor would keep the two jobs in sync)
    services:
      postgres:
        image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/postgres:17.6
        ports: ["5432:5432"]
        env: { POSTGRES_DB: rhino_cloud, POSTGRES_USER: rhino, POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${{ secrets.CLOUD_TEST_POSTGRES_PASSWORD }}" }
        command: -c fsync=off -c synchronous_commit=off -c full_page_writes=off
        options: --health-cmd pg_isready --health-interval 10s --health-timeout 5s --health-retries 5

notes.text: The job id. Other jobs refer to it by this name.
The name GitHub shows, and the name a ruleset would require later (G7-31).
fcp's self-hosted runner set, like every other cloud job.
Wait for the change detector.
Run on main always, and on a branch only when cloud code changed.
The settings module picks its environment from ENV.
Loads settings_test.py, which uses a fast MD5 password hasher.
The service container is reachable on localhost.
The password comes from a repo secret, never from the file.
The test job's env block has about 30 more lines. A YAML anchor would let both jobs share one copy.
The service container. GitHub starts it before the steps and removes it after.
The same Postgres version as the test job, from AWS's public mirror of Docker Hub.
Turn off disk safety. The database is thrown away, so speed matters more than durability.
The job waits until pg_isready says the server accepts connections.

sections.h: The CI job, part 2: run and keep the reports
p: The steps install exactly the locked packages of the api-tests group and run the layer with four workers. When the job fails, the reports folder is uploaded, so you can download failures.md and junit.xml from the run page.
The job leaves out the NVFlare venv steps that the test job has. If a test needs NVFlare, it belongs in rhinoCore/tests, not here.
sections.because: We upload the reports only on failure, because a green run needs no evidence and an artifact costs storage.

code.text:
steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
      - name: Run the API layer
        working-directory: cloud/rhinoCloud
        run: |
          uv sync --frozen --group api-tests --no-install-project
          .venv/bin/pytest tests_api -n 4 --junitxml=reports/junit.xml
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: failure()
        with: { name: api-tests-reports, path: cloud/rhinoCloud/reports/ }

notes.text: The job's steps run in order on the runner.
Check out this commit.
Install Python 3.13, the version cloud/rhinoCloud requires.
Run the next commands inside cloud/rhinoCloud.
Install exactly what uv.lock says (like npm ci), only the api-tests group, without installing the project itself.
Run the layer with 4 xdist workers and write a JUnit report.
Upload a folder from the runner so you can download it later.
Only when an earlier step failed.
The artifact's name and the folder that holds failures.md and junit.xml.

callout.text: Agents never change the checks they are judged by. Ask DevOps to add cloud-ci.yml, tests_api/pytest.ini and tests_api/conftest.py to the protected paths (the G0 and G3 walls). Then an agent PR that edits them fails the locked-checks check.

p: An agent fixes its own mistakes only when it can read the failure. A pytest log of 3,000 lines fills its context. G7-12 adds a small pytest plugin that writes one page, reports/failures.md, after every run.

A pytest plugin is a module with functions whose names pytest knows, called hooks (pytest hooks, not Claude Code hooks). pytest_sessionfinish runs once, after all tests. Register the module in tests_api/conftest.py with pytest_plugins = ["plugins.agent_report"].
sections.because: We read the results from pytest's terminal reporter, because it already holds every failed report, also from xdist workers.

code.text:
import os
from pathlib import Path

MAX_FAILURES = 20
TAIL_LINES = 40


def pytest_sessionfinish(session, exitstatus):
    if hasattr(session.config, "workerinput"):  # an xdist worker: the controller writes the report
        return
    stats = session.config.pluginmanager.get_plugin("terminalreporter").stats
    failed = [r for r in stats.get("failed", []) + stats.get("error", []) if r.when in ("setup", "call")]
    seed = session.config.getoption("randomly_seed", default=None)
    lines = [f"# API tests: {len(failed)} failing (seed {seed})", ""]

notes.text: os reads the environment variable for the report folder.
At most 20 failures on the page. More than that is a broken setup, not 20 bugs.
The last 40 lines of each traceback, where the error usually is.
The hook pytest calls once at the end of the session, with the session and the exit status.
Only xdist workers have workerinput. Workers return; the controller process writes the one report.
pytest's reporter plugin. Its stats dict maps an outcome (passed, failed, error) to a list of reports.
Failed tests plus errors, only from setup (a fixture broke) or call (the test body broke). Teardown noise is left out.
The seed pytest-randomly used, so the rerun command can repeat the same order.
The page starts with a heading: how many failed and with which seed.

sections.h: failures.md, part 2: one block per failure
p: Each failure becomes a short block. It holds the node id, the file and line, the first error line, the traceback's tail and a rerun command. JUnit XML (lesson p10-6) keeps everything else.

The seed matters. With --randomly-seed=1009, pytest-randomly shuffles the tests in the same order on every run and reseeds random, Faker and factory_boy. So the rerun command reproduces the failure. Decide with the guild whether the nightly uses a new seed each night to find order bugs.
sections.because: We print a ready-to-paste rerun command, because an agent that guesses the command wastes a turn and may run the wrong tests.

code.text:
for report in failed[:MAX_FAILURES]:
        crash = getattr(report.longrepr, "reprcrash", None)
        lines += [
            f"## {report.nodeid}",
            f"- where: {crash.path}:{crash.lineno}" if crash else "- where: fixture or setup error",
            f"- error: {crash.message.splitlines()[0]}" if crash else "",
            "```",
            *report.longreprtext.splitlines()[-TAIL_LINES:],
            "```",
            f"- rerun: `cd cloud/rhinoCloud && uv run --group api-tests pytest tests_api/{report.nodeid} --randomly-seed={seed}`",
            "",
        ]
    if len(failed) > MAX_FAILURES:
        lines.append(f"{len(failed) - MAX_FAILURES} more failures are in reports/junit.xml")
    out = Path(os.environ.get("API_TEST_REPORT_DIR", "reports"))
    out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (out / "failures.md").write_text("\n".join(lines) if failed else "# API tests: all passed\n")

notes.text: Loop over the first 20 failures.
reprcrash is where the error was raised: path, line number and message. A setup error may not have one, so default to None.
A heading per failure: the node id, file::function[case].
file:line of the crash, or a note that a fixture or setup step failed.
Only the first line of the error message.
The last 40 lines of the full traceback, inside a fenced code block.
A command that reruns exactly this test with the same seed.
Say how many more failures exist and where to find them.
The folder is reports/ unless the environment variable says otherwise.
Create the folder; no error if it exists.
Write the page, or one line that says all passed. A stale page from an earlier run is always overwritten.

sections.see:
# API tests: 1 failing (seed 1009)

## test_smoke.py::test_lists_projects
- where: tests_api/test_smoke.py:14
- error: AssertionError: assert 2 == 3
- rerun: `cd cloud/rhinoCloud && uv run --group api-tests pytest tests_api/test_smoke.py::test_lists_projects --randomly-seed=1009`

p: The last two Poe tasks go into the root pyproject.toml, next to backend-integration-tests. api-test runs everything in parallel. api-test-affected runs only the tests whose code paths your change touched, with pytest-testmon (lesson p10-2). Add pytest-testmon to the api-tests group and .testmondata and reports/ to .gitignore.

testmon sees only Python code that tests execute. Migrations, fixture files and the conftest are read during setup, so a change there would look like no change at all. That is why poe verify (lesson g7-5) runs the full layer when one of those changes. The G3 nightly sandbox image runs api-test-affected once on main, so every VM starts with a fresh .testmondata.
sections.because: We give both tasks the same seed and options, because the same failing test should look the same in both.

notes.text: A banner comment, in the style the root pyproject already uses for its task groups.

A cmd task: pytest in the api-tests group with one worker per CPU (-n auto). It adds the fixed seed, a JUnit report, quiet output and short tracebacks. cwd makes it run from cloud/rhinoCloud, and help is what poe prints in its task list.
No -n here: the set is small, and testmon with xdist is not yet checked for the pinned version.
The same command with --testmon instead of -n auto and the JUnit report.

callout.text: Prove testmon on history before you trust it. Take 5 recent cloud PRs and check that the affected set included every test that failed in CI. Put the answer in the G7-13 PR.

lab.title: Read the setup tests_api builds on, in your fcp checkout
youNeed: Python 3 (python3 is on every Mac with git's Command Line Tools)

worked.see: A number in the 220s (the tickets counted 228 on main on 12 Oct). Each one would run once per worker without the template.
The groups grpc-stub-gen, dev, lint, test and integration-tests. There is no api-tests group yet; G7-02 adds it.
[pytest] with markers local, ci_only, nightly, testing_trace_id and connect_api: the integration-test markers tests_api must not inherit.
The POSTGRES_* variables, image: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/postgres:17.6 and -c fsync=off: the block G7-03 copies.

worked.do: grep -rn CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/tests | wc -l && grep -rn patch cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/tests | grep -c AgentRpcClient

python3 -c "import hashlib, pathlib; m=''.join(sorted(p.name for p in pathlib.Path('cloud/rhinoCloud/rhinoCore/migrations').glob('[0-9]*.py'))); print('api_tpl_' + hashlib.sha1(m.encode()).hexdigest()[:12])"
worked.see: api_tpl_ followed by 12 hex characters, for example api_tpl_3f9c0a1b7d2e. This is the template name the conftest would use today.

lab.faded: Repeat the last command, but add one made-up migration name to the string before hashing (for example m + '9999_fake.py'). Predict first: same name or a new one? The command to write is left to you.
lab.alone: Read the test job's env block in cloud-ci.yml. Write down which variables the api-tests job must copy so the settings module can import. Start with ENV, DJANGO_SECRET_KEY and the POSTGRES_* lines. Then say which ones it can leave out because tests_api uses fakes, not MinIO or Redis.
lab.done: You can name the migration count, the missing group, today's template name and the env lines the new job needs.

quiz.q: A teammate writes a test that checks one model method, with no request. Where does it go?

options.text: tests_api/, because new tests use pytest.
options.why: G7-01 splits by kind of test, not by age: endpoint tests go to tests_api/.

options.text: rhinoCore/tests, on manage.py test with CommonRhinoTestCase.
options.why: Model and service unit tests stay where they are; tests_api is for tests that call an endpoint and check the response.

options.text: rhinoCore/integration-tests, so it runs on QA.
options.why: That folder is for tests that need a real environment; a model method needs none.

quiz.q: Why does the conftest take pg_advisory_lock(7007) before checking for the template?

options.text: To stop tests in other CI jobs from reading the template.
options.why: Each CI job has its own throw-away Postgres; the lock is about workers inside one run.

options.text: Because Postgres requires a lock before CREATE DATABASE.
options.why: It does not; the lock is our own choice.

options.text: Because four xdist workers start at once, and only one may run the migrations.
options.why: The others wait on the lock, then find the template and copy it.

quiz.q: You change a fixture JSON file in rhinoCore/fixtures. What does poe api-test-affected run?

options.text: Possibly nothing, because testmon only sees Python code that tests execute.
options.why: Fixtures, migrations and the conftest are read during setup, so poe verify runs the full layer when they change.

options.text: Every test that loads the fixture, because testmon tracks file reads.
options.why: testmon tracks executed Python lines, not data files.

options.text: The whole layer, because a fixture change clears .testmondata.
options.why: Nothing clears it; that is why verify checks these paths itself.

words.plain: The new tests_api/ folder: pytest tests that send requests through the cloud's API in-process and check the response.
The pytest-django fixture that creates the test database once per session; G7-02 overrides it to copy a template.
A named lock in Postgres that code takes and releases on purpose; here it lets one worker build the template.
A container GitHub Actions starts next to a job (here Postgres) and removes when the job ends.
The one-page report the agent_report plugin writes: per failure the place, the error, the traceback tail and a rerun command.
A set random seed (1009) so pytest-randomly shuffles tests the same way every run and a failure reproduces.

remember: Migrate once into a template, copy it per worker, and give the agent one page with a rerun command.
